result_text:
Template literals are now masked the same way as `"..."` and `'...'` literals when units are compared for duplication. I didn't add a test for the new case. I ran the existing unit, duplication and JavaScript tests in `codeanalyzer`, and they passed.

The change is one line in `extraCleanContent` in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/units/CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java`:

```java
cleanedContent = cleanedContent.replaceAll("`.*?`", "``");
```

It sits right after the single-quote replacement, so it applies to everything that extractor handles. `` `Hello alpha ${name}` `` and `` `Hello beta ${name}` `` now both become ` `` `. Two such functions end up with the same normalized body and are reported as one duplicated unit. A difference in the code outside the literal still keeps them apart.

Template literals that span several lines aren't masked, because the match works line by line, as it does for the other quote types.
